plugins.name: adr
plugins.description: Architecture decision records held as beads `decision` beads, registered as decisions land rather than reconstructed at closeout. The bead is the record; a pre-commit hook projects every closed decision into a MADR file under `docs/adr/` so the choice is readable in a PR by anyone without beads installed. Ships steering for when a choice earns a record, a skill for registering one, the renderer, and a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` fragment. Enforcement is native: `bd create --validate` and `bd lint` require a rationale and a rejected alternative, and `bd supersede` records replacement as a typed edge. Requires `bd`; the hook exits 0 without it.

plugins.name: agent-adversarial-challenger
plugins.description: Read-only adversarial challenger: independently stress-tests any claim, plan, design, hypothesis, decision, or conclusion -- technical or not -- by attacking its assumptions and returning evidence-backed counter-arguments and alternatives, without changing anything. The critic half of a generate/critique loop; debugging escalation, debate devil's-advocate, research and decision review are all applications.

plugins.name: agent-builder
plugins.description: Implementation subagent for bounded code changes, tests, and refactors within a defined scope. Ships `builder`, which runs in one of two modes the caller must name: `direct-edit` (edits the caller's tree in place; the caller commits) or `isolated` (own git worktree, commits continuously, hands back a reviewable branch). It refuses to start when the mode is unstated, because the two modes fail in opposite and unrecoverable directions.

plugins.name: agent-builder-high
plugins.description: Escalated implementation agent for complex bounded work, difficult debugging, and cross-module behaviour changes. Ships `builder-high`, the escalation tier above `agent-builder`'s `builder`.

plugins.name: agent-conformance
plugins.description: Deterministic conformance harness for agent contract testing: check coverage and drift, stage per-case sandboxes, assert captured replies, and assemble run reports -- no LLM required for the engine.

plugins.name: agent-explorer
plugins.description: Read-only exploration agent for bounded code and configuration discovery.

plugins.name: agent-external-repo-worker
plugins.description: Subagent that works inside an external repository outside the caller project. Handles isolated clone or reuse, convention discovery, bounded edits, local verification, and delegated publish or PR work.

plugins.name: agent-hook-contract
plugins.description: Cross-tool agent hook contract for Claude Code and Codex CLI: supported events, matcher behavior, payloads, decisions, trust, and runtime limits, plus the authoring rules this repo holds its hooks to. Hooks are written in Python unless the script only forwards to one command: a hook that parses shell with grep and sed is a tokenizer without a lexer, and every gap is a bypass. Python is also faster once a hook touches jq, since one jq spawn costs more than the whole bash-vs-Python startup gap. Covers the per-call performance budget (no uv run on a per-tool-call hook, stdlib only on the hot path, in-process repo root discovery, batched git calls, cheap pre-parse bail) and the reliability rules (fail open, never emit ask, write denials to the model, accept a string tool_input, self-filter inside the script). Documentation only.

plugins.name: agent-management
plugins.description: Manage APM-backed project agents, skills, hooks, steering, bundles, and package dependencies. Use when a repo already has or is about to get apm.yml and the task is to add, update, remove, install, compile, patch, or audit agentic assets.

plugins.name: agent-operator
plugins.description: Mechanical operator agent for tiny commands, formatting, and inventory steps.

plugins.name: agent-pr-reviewer
plugins.description: Subagent that reviews pull requests for code quality, security, and best practices.

plugins.name: agent-quality-guards
plugins.description: Read-only quality-guard subagents for bounded triage: docs-guard checks scoped documentation and documentation lint findings, lint-guard validates and normalizes lint reports, data-metrics-summarizer compacts large logs and metrics, maintenance-metrics-reader snapshots repository maintenance health (stale branches, worktrees, lock states), and reviewer-mechanics smoke-checks scoped diffs for mechanical issues. All five reply with bounded, capped verdict lines and never edit files.

plugins.name: agent-reasoner
plugins.description: Read-only reasoning agent for exceptional architecture, policy, and adversarial questions.

plugins.name: agent-reviewer-high
plugins.description: Adversarial read-only reviewer for security-sensitive and broad-impact changes.

plugins.name: agent-reviewer-low
plugins.description: Mechanical read-only reviewer for tiny changes with explicit criteria.

plugins.name: agentic-maintenance
plugins.description: Maintain your agentic assets: audit and optimize steering, write new skills, with the coder and PR reviewer agents.

plugins.name: audit-steering
plugins.description: Audit agent rules, hooks, skills, and guardrails for drift, duplication, stale files, and token waste.

plugins.name: beads
plugins.description: Beads (bd) conventions for persistent task DAGs, atomic claims, native reply threads, decision records, ambiguity handling, actor identity, JSON envelopes, and Dolt sync. Steering separates local comments from cross-boundary decisions and harness wakes from persisted messages, and owns the carrier doctrine that dependent packages map onto. A build-formula skill covers formula authoring: conditional steps, gates, composition, and the assertions that prove a formula pours the DAG it declares. A guard denies mutating `gh issue` commands in Beads repositories. Opt-in sync hooks prefer native Dolt sync -- pull at session start, a detached push at session end once a `git push --dry-run` probe confirms it goes through, with a configurable pusher for hosts that need a wrapper -- and fall back to JSONL over ordinary git otherwise. The same session-start hook reports when Dolt history has grown enough to trim, and never trims it. Global `bd setup` wires session start; `bd init --skip-hooks` initializes repositories. Requires Beads >= 1.1.0 and python3 on PATH, and activates only in repositories with `.beads/`.

plugins.name: brownfield-project
plugins.description: Retrofit an existing repository into APM-managed agentic tooling without broad scaffolding. Use when onboarding, ingesting, or repairing a brownfield repo, especially when the agent must first discover project purpose, requirements, and workflow needs interactively.

plugins.name: catchup
plugins.description: Resume interrupted project work from the best handover and, in beads (bd) repos, live task state -- after context loss, /clear, or a continue/resume request, including repos with open beads but no handover file.

plugins.name: chezmoi-editor
plugins.description: Edit chezmoi-managed dotfiles from their authoritative source files. Use when changing dotfiles, global agent/tool config, templates, private files, symlinked config, or any live target that may be managed by chezmoi.

plugins.name: cmux
plugins.description: cmux terminal control bundle: vendored user-facing skills that teach agents to drive and configure the cmux macOS terminal via its socket CLI -- topology and routing (windows, workspaces, panes, surfaces), customization, settings, socket policy, Ghostty rendering config, keyboard shortcuts, diagnostics, and shared behavior. Contributor skills (architecture, backend, release, testing) are omitted. Third-party (manaflow-ai/cmux publishes no APM/marketplace manifest); referenced as raw GitHub skill paths, same pattern as the other external bundles.

plugins.name: code-intelligence
plugins.description: Codebase understanding toolkit: semantic Serena routing, web-fetch, the PR reviewer agent, and project-structure steering. The SubagentStart context injector requires python3 on PATH.

plugins.name: core
plugins.description: Baseline bundle for any repo: layers the project-lifecycle, code-intelligence, and agentic-maintenance sub-bundles, plus resume-session and the Matt Pocock grill workflows.

plugins.name: data-ai
plugins.description: Data and AI toolkit: data steering for LLM applications, data engineering, MLOps, and databases.

plugins.name: debate
plugins.description: Deep tradeoff analysis for architectural decisions, technology choices, and feature proposals. Tests an idea from both sides before recommending a path.

plugins.name: dep-update
plugins.description: Research each dependency's current latest version against installed lockfile pins, classify patch/minor/major bumps by safety, surface CVEs via native scanners, and produce a severity-grouped cited upgrade plan. Applies only patch and minor bumps interactively -- one at a time behind a per-bump confirm; major bumps are advisory-only and never applied. Reads .project-setup/ answers.toml opportunistically; never writes it.

plugins.name: dependency-quality
plugins.description: Dependency hygiene bundle: nudges to investigate a dependency before adding it. Manifest-edit and latest-version guidance lives in steering-toolchain-defaults. CVE scanning is deliberately absent -- vulnerability discovery is time-based rather than commit-based, so it belongs to continuous alerts (Dependabot or Renovate) plus a CI job, neither of which an on-demand skill can substitute for.

plugins.name: diagrams
plugins.description: Diagram generation bundle for editable draw.io diagrams, visual Excalidraw diagrams, and D2 architecture or flow diagrams.

plugins.name: eli5
plugins.description: Explain a topic at five depth levels, from metaphor to frontier, for layered understanding of unfamiliar concepts.

plugins.name: find-tools
plugins.description: Discover and vet reusable skills, agents, MCP servers, connectors, and APM packages. Use when the user asks to find a capability, compare tools, fill a marketplace gap, evaluate an external package, or decide whether to adopt, wrap, fork, reject, or build.

plugins.name: frontend
plugins.description: Frontend development and design toolkit: the Playwright browser skill, frontend steering, and external design/build skills (Impeccable, Interface Design, Stitch).

plugins.name: go-quality
plugins.description: Run Go format, lint, and test checks with the project toolchain.

plugins.name: goal-writer
plugins.description: Turn a vague goal prompt into a structured, actionable goal -- with outcomes, concrete results, measurable KPIs, validation, and verifiable exit conditions -- saved as a context doc, then emit a self-sufficient /goal block that references the doc and tests done-ness via AND-joined exit conditions.

plugins.name: handover
plugins.description: Save a self-contained recovery prompt to the shared handover store when pausing work, switching context, preserving unfinished state, or handing off to another session. In beads (bd) repos, flushes task state into beads and keeps the file narrative-only.

plugins.name: hooks-attribution-guard
plugins.description: Advises against AI authorship attribution in git commits so the human stays the sole author of record. Covers agent trailers from any vendor (Co-Authored-By / Signed-off-by / Assisted-by naming Claude, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Devin, aider, Gemini, OpenHands, Windsurf and others, or pointing at an agent noreply address), "Generated with/by" phrases, agent signature URLs, robot-emoji signature lines, and hyphenated AI-assisted/AI-generated qualifiers. Emits a non-blocking advisory (allow + additionalContext, exit 0); a commit message is trivially fixable, so it never blocks. Scoped to authorship constructs, so ordinary work that merely names an agent or a model ("fix AI model loading bug", "bump anthropic sdk") is not flagged. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-bash-safety
plugins.description: Bash safety guard tuned for autonomous agents, in one Python module with a real shell tokenizer. Denies only the unrecoverable: rm -rf on the filesystem root, a home root, or a system-critical tree (BS-4/BS-8), rm -rf whose target hides behind an unexpanded variable so the guard cannot verify it (BS-9), mkfs (BS-5), dd onto a real block device while allowing the pseudo-devices (BS-6), and the sandbox-bypass flag (BS-3). Warns without blocking on a curl-to-shell pipe, sudo with a destructive verb, and rm -rf outside the git working tree (BS-7, BS-10). Anything inside the working tree is assumed git-recoverable and passes silently, so wiping node_modules or a build directory says nothing. Because the command is tokenized rather than pattern-matched, wrapper prefixes, env assignments, leading tabs, quoted targets, flags after the target, path traversal, subshells, loop bodies, and a rebasing cd are all covered by construction. Never emits "ask". Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-chezmoi-guard
plugins.description: PreToolUse advisory (non-blocking) for writes to files chezmoi ACTUALLY manages (exact membership in `chezmoi managed`, 60s cache). A managed target is a real file rather than a symlink to its source, so a direct edit succeeds and is then reverted by the next `chezmoi apply` with no error and no diff; this names that before the edit lands. Emits permissionDecision:"allow" + additionalContext pointing at the source -- the operation proceeds. Bound to the write tools (apply_patch/Edit/Write/MultiEdit), so a redirect-based shell write is not covered. A PostToolUse advisory additionally reports when an edit landed on an applied target rather than its source, names the template when the source is one, and lists what is already uncommitted in the chezmoi source repo; it runs no git or chezmoi write command. Unmanaged paths and paths merely mentioned in a patch body are silent. Requires python3 on PATH. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-close-keywords
plugins.description: Fixes the GitHub "comma-list close" quirk, where a closing keyword binds to only the FIRST issue in a list (Closes #1, #2, #3 closes just #1). A shared normalizer distributes the keyword across every issue in a contiguous list (-> Closes #1, closes #2, closes #3) for close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, resolve/resolves/resolved. Two delivery layers: a pre-commit commit-msg hook that rewrites the message in place (tool-agnostic), and a PreToolUse guard on `gh pr create`/`gh pr edit` that emits a non-blocking advisory (allow + additionalContext carrying the corrected body) when a malformed comma-list close is detected. Requires python3 on PATH. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-git-safety
plugins.description: Git safety guard for autonomous agents, in one Python module with a real shell tokenizer. Denies exactly one thing: a destructive op aimed at another working tree through an unexpanded variable or ~, where the guard cannot resolve which tree is affected (GS-2). Everything else is non-blocking. reset --hard, checkout --, restore, and clean -f warn only when repository state shows work would really be lost (GS-3, GS-5, GS-6), so a clean tree stays silent and an untracked-only tree does not trip the reset rules. push --force always warns, because the loss is on the remote where local state cannot answer for it (GS-4). branch -D, tag -d, stash drop, and worktree remove --force pass silently, all being reflog-recoverable. State reads happen once, and only after a destructive verb matches. An unreadable tree warns rather than staying quiet. Never emits "ask". Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-package-investigate
plugins.description: Non-blocking PreToolUse Bash hook that nudges the agent to investigate a dependency's trustworthiness, maintenance, quality, popularity, and alternatives BEFORE adding/installing it (lighter review for update/upgrade/remove). Requires python3 on PATH. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-quality
plugins.description: Non-blocking quality advisory on edits. Accumulates edited files and changed lines across a session and suggests targeted checks (ruff, gofmt, cargo fmt, biome) once the change is large enough to warrant one, then holds a cooldown so it does not nag. Commit-time formatting is deliberately not covered: that is the pre-commit framework's stage, and this hook advises per language only where the framework does not already run a checker for it, which needs both an installed framework hook and a config naming that checker. Language selection reads .agents/hooks/quality-languages, then AGENTIC_QUALITY_LANGS, then marker files, so an unrecognised project is silent rather than guessed at. Never denies. Thresholds via AGENTIC_QUALITY_ADVISORY_LINES, _FILES, _COOLDOWN_SECONDS. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-serena
plugins.description: Serena lifecycle hooks for Claude Code and Codex. Activates Serena at session start, reminds agents to use symbolic tools, and clears hook state at session end without configuring MCP transport.

plugins.name: hooks-subagent-fork
plugins.description: PreToolUse:Agent deny gate rejecting Codex spawn_agent calls whose fork_turns is "all", omitted (Codex defaults omitted to a full-history fork), or above the numeric maximum (default 3, SUBAGENT_FORK_GUARD_MAX overrides). Denials carry the corrected call format. A SubagentStart hook injects the fork_turns="none" discipline into spawning subagents, and an always-on instruction carries the same rule in the main session. Codex-only: Claude has no fork_turns concept, so the package does not target Claude at all. The hook fails open on malformed input. Requires python3 on PATH.

plugins.name: hooks-subagent-model
plugins.description: Claude PreToolUse:Agent deny gate requiring an explicit model when a spawn would inherit the parent session model. It allows explicit models and pinned agent types. Denials include routing guidance. SUBAGENT_MODEL_GUARD_INHERIT_TYPES adds unpinned types. The hook fails open on malformed input. Reasoning effort stays in reusable agent definitions because Agent calls have no effort field. Codex does not receive this hook.

plugins.name: hooks-subagent-worktree
plugins.description: Non-blocking worktree-isolation advisory on every subagent spawn. A PreToolUse:Agent hook injects a short reminder -- if the subagent WRITES files and runs in parallel with other writers, pass `isolation:"worktree"` (Claude branches it from your current HEAD); a read-only, different-repo, or lone-writer subagent needs none -- and if it does run isolated, to COMMIT before finishing so the worktree branch retains the work. It NEVER denies a spawn (superseding the 1.x deny-gate, which guessed wrong and blocked legitimate work) and stays silent once isolation is already declared. Claude-only (the Agent spawn tool is Claude-specific); the Codex variant is a no-op. Requires python3 on PATH.

plugins.name: hooks-worktrunk
plugins.description: Enforces Worktrunk as the worktree-management interface for Claude and Codex. A cross-runtime PreToolUse guard denies direct git worktree and gh pr checkout commands with the equivalent wt command, a PreToolUse:Agent guard denies harness isolation:"worktree" in favor of a parent-prepared checkout, and Claude-only WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove handlers route the native worktree lifecycle through wt. A SessionStart sweep reports Worktrunk worktrees that are abandoned -- clean, fully pushed, and untouched for weeks -- and reclaims their git-ignored build output; it never removes a worktree or branch, leaving that to `wt remove`, which already refuses an unmerged branch. Steering and config templates cover official plugins, agent checkout isolation, lifecycle hook ownership, repository-scoped build targets, copy-ignored warm starts, deterministic dev-server ports, aliases, and LLM commit generation.

plugins.name: matt-skills
plugins.description: Bundle of Matt Pocock's engineering and productivity skills: grilling, grill-with-docs, tdd, to-prd, to-issues, triage, improve-codebase-architecture, and setup.

plugins.name: mcp-codebase-memory
plugins.description: MCP server package for the Codebase Memory MCP, providing graph-aware project orientation (symbol search, call paths, code snippets). Available but not wired by default; requires explicit installation and index build.

plugins.name: mcp-context7
plugins.description: MCP server package for Context7, providing current library and framework documentation lookups.

plugins.name: mcp-fetcher
plugins.description: MCP server package for Fetcher, providing direct web-page retrieval for coding agents.

plugins.name: mcp-package-version
plugins.description: MCP server for package version discovery

plugins.name: mcp-playwright
plugins.description: MCP server package for Playwright, providing stateful browser automation and in-browser UI verification. The server inlines the accessibility tree on every action, so prefer `playwright-cli` (see the `playwright` skill) for scripted flows and keep this for loops that need the model reasoning over page structure turn by turn. Do not pass `--snapshot-mode none`: element refs come from snapshots, so it removes the ability to interact.

plugins.name: mcp-repomix
plugins.description: MCP server package for Repomix, providing bulk repository snapshots for analysis and review. The PostToolUse snapshot-refresh hook requires python3 on PATH.

plugins.name: mcp-serena
plugins.description: MCP server package for Serena semantic code tools. The launcher shares one Serena backend across agents in the same checkout, isolates linked worktrees, and applies resource and capacity limits to worktree backends.

plugins.name: mcp-tauri
plugins.description: Tauri MCP workflow guidance for building, testing, debugging, and driving Tauri v2 apps through an MCP runtime supplied separately by the environment.

plugins.name: orchestrate
plugins.description: Coordinates parallel subagents through Beads-backed DAGs, claims, threaded replies, decisions, review, and merge state. Supports exact, specialist, generic-pull, writable-fallback, and read-only research dispatch. Bundles coder (with effort-tier variants), researcher, reviewer, advisor, shepherd, and scribe. Quality triage roles (docs-guard, lint-guard, data-metrics-summarizer, maintenance-metrics-reader, reviewer-mechanics) come from the agent-quality-guards dependency. Includes deterministic scope, discovery, claim, message, decision, queue, and conflict scripts plus shared PR shepherd landing safeguards. Requires the bd CLI.

plugins.name: planning-product
plugins.description: Planning and product toolkit: the debate, eli5, and web-fetch skills plus Matt's PRD, issue-writing, TDD, triage, and architecture-improvement workflows.

plugins.name: playwright
plugins.description: Automate browser tasks with Playwright, routing between the two interfaces by context cost. The `playwright-cli` path writes the accessibility snapshot to a file and returns a path (402 bytes against 33,011 inlined by MCP on the same page) while keeping full interaction and cross-invocation state. The MCP server is reserved for loops that need the model to reason over page structure turn by turn: exploratory automation, self-healing tests, long autonomous sessions.

plugins.name: pr-shepherd
plugins.description: Cross-session PR shepherd with beads as its durable state store. It validates exact check and head identity, honors persisted merge-slot order, merges with an atomic head guard, proves exact content on the final landing branch, and reconciles partial bounce writes through durable receipts. Stacked PRs remain open after their intermediate merge until their content reaches the landing branch. The skill and standalone agent optionally consume release-queue-watch records with crash-replay receipts. Requires bd, gh, git, and jq; inert in repositories without .beads/.

plugins.name: presentation
plugins.description: Presentation bundle for general decks, Marp slides, and PowerPoint template workflows.

plugins.name: project-lifecycle
plugins.description: Day-to-day project lifecycle workflows: resume work after interruption (catchup), write handovers, and run verification. Bundles the matching skills, git-workflow steering, and the PR reviewer agent.

plugins.name: python-quality
plugins.description: Run Python format, lint, type-check, and test commands with the project toolchain.

plugins.name: release-please
plugins.description: Drive releases with googleapis/release-please. Use for any release, tagging, changelog, or version-bump work, and whenever the repo has a release-please-config.json / .release-please-manifest.json or a release-please workflow -- then following release-please is mandatory. Also use to set up release-please in a repo. Covers setup, the git/commit process, publishing, monorepo/manifest config, and diagnosing and recovering stuck or botched releases. Ships one Python script (requires python3 on PATH) serving both a warn-only cross-tool advisory hook, which never blocks, and a `detect` subcommand that reports how the repo configures release-please.

plugins.name: release-queue-watch
plugins.description: Runs a signed local GitHub webhook receiver that emits deterministic PR lifecycle records, tracks agent-owned priority and merge-slot state, and retains Octokit REST reconciliation without mutating GitHub or Beads.

plugins.name: resume-cv
plugins.description: CV / career-resume bundle: focused resume-tailoring and broad career-support workflows. Renamed from `resume` to avoid a namespace collision with `resume-session` (which resumes a prior coding SESSION, not a CV).

plugins.name: resume-session
plugins.description: Resume a previous agent session in the current repository from its transcript, reading only the latest context incrementally instead of reloading the full history. Discovers prior Claude Code and Codex sessions, summarizes the leftoff state, confirms ambiguities, then continues the work.

plugins.name: review
plugins.description: Code review and verification toolkit: the verify skill and the PR reviewer agent. Language-specific quality checks live in the language-<lang> bundles.

plugins.name: rust-quality
plugins.description: Run Rust format, lint, and test checks with the project toolchain.

plugins.name: session-review
plugins.description: Audit the ending session for corrections, lessons, unresolved TODOs, and follow-up work, then recommend handoffs to `handover`, `audit-steering`, or `write-agentic`. Use when the user says wrap up, review this session, what did we learn, or before a handover.

plugins.name: sniff
plugins.description: Refactoring auditor. Detects code smells, tech debt, and non-idiomatic code across 21 languages and formats, maps each finding to refactoring.guru smells, patterns, and techniques, stress-tests every recommendation with a built-in adversarial pragmatism critic, and produces a prioritized refactoring plan (impact, value, cost, severity, backwards-compatibility). Drives each language toolchain's own linters and analyzers (opportunistic, never required) with a guided first-run installer. Advisory by default; applies low-risk refactors only on explicit approval behind a verification re-run. Standalone: no APM dependencies.

plugins.name: speckit
plugins.description: SpecKit mechanism: the six SpecKit agents and the bugfix and setup skills. Opt into the opinionated layers separately: steering-speckit (the mandatory-gated workflow); workflow gates are beads gate beads provisioned by the speckit-beads formula during setup.

plugins.name: speckit-beads
plugins.description: Beads-native SpecKit workflow: ships the speckit-feature bd formula (the SpecKit phase spine as a molecule DAG with human gates at clarify approval, analyze approval, and verify sign-off), steering that maps one spec dir to one molecule root epic and implementation task beads to the implement step, and a PreToolUse guard that denies every Write/Edit to specs/*/tasks.md when a beads workspace is active -- task state lives in beads and tasks.md is never authored (reads stay allowed for legacy migration). Replaces the archived speckit-gate gates.yaml engine. Requires the bd CLI (gastownhall/beads >= 1.1.0) and python3 on PATH; guard and steering are inert in repos without .beads/. Install the formula by copying formulas/speckit-feature.formula.toml into the repo's .beads/formulas/.

plugins.name: steering-architecture
plugins.description: Cross-cutting design steering: compose over fork, keep generic cores case-agnostic, and make structural invariants a verifiable diff guard. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-backend
plugins.description: Opinionated backend conventions: service/function/worker runtime shape, API and cross-boundary contract rules, and background-job (queue, event, scheduled) patterns. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-data
plugins.description: Opinionated data conventions: data ownership, database assets, migrations, pipelines, and notebook practices. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-delivery
plugins.description: Opinionated delivery cadence: work like a developer who commits continuously. Commit and push after every meaningful, self-contained step; keep commits atomic; leave no unpushed local work stranded in a local or disposable worktree. Always-on steering. Opt-in.

plugins.name: steering-docs-specs
plugins.description: Spec and SpecKit workflow conventions: spec modes, specs/ placement, and .specify/ asset separation. Doc-writing style rules live in the slopvac package (srobroek/slopvac). Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-frontend
plugins.description: Opinionated frontend conventions: framework choice by surface (React/Vue/Next/Astro), UI library picks, app vs server state, and browser verification expectations. Opt-in steering -- install to adopt these frontend defaults.

plugins.name: steering-git-workflow
plugins.description: Git workflow policy: branch discipline, ship-path choice (merge vs PR), merge flags, draft-first PRs, Beads body linkage, and pre-push verification. Ships a dual-runtime PreToolUse blocker for non-draft or unlinked PR creation. Replaces the retired commit-push-* skills and git nudge hooks.

plugins.name: steering-global-bootstrap
plugins.description: User-scope bootstrap steering that keeps reusable agentic assets in APM packages and limits chezmoi to session profiles and dotfile management. Install globally; project behavior remains project-local.

plugins.name: steering-infrastructure
plugins.description: Opinionated infrastructure conventions: platform code, IaC, deployment config, CI/CD, environments, and observability. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-multi-agent
plugins.description: Multi-agent coexistence steering: tolerate concurrent agents and human authors in the same repo or worktree without reverting or reporting their benign changes, and escape interference (including branch switches underneath you) by moving to a Worktrunk checkout instead of fighting back. Always-on steering. Opt-in.

plugins.name: steering-pragmatic
plugins.description: Opinionated pragmatic working style: prioritize accuracy, calibration, and decision usefulness over agreeableness. Analytical and direct by default; distinguish facts from assumptions; avoid hype and sycophancy. Includes code economy defaults (prefer deletion, stdlib, and minimal solutions over new abstractions) and comment discipline. Always-on steering as main-session instructions, plus a SubagentStart hook that injects the same discipline into every subagent in MUST register. Requires python3 on PATH. Opt-in.

plugins.name: steering-project-structure
plugins.description: Opt-in steering: capability-first repository structure and ownership conventions -- repo layout, ownership boundaries, shared libraries, contracts, and where docs/specs/tools live.

plugins.name: steering-speckit
plugins.description: Opinionated SpecKit workflow steering: the mandatory-gated Phase 1/2/3 DAG, human-gating rules, and command reference. Names which phases produce a decision record and defers the format, path, and gate to the adr package. Opt-in -- install alongside the speckit package to adopt this specific spec-driven process.

plugins.name: steering-subagent-routing
plugins.description: Opt-in steering: model routing and verification policy for delegated subagents -- when to delegate, model/effort choice, parallel work, and who owns verification.

plugins.name: steering-toolchain-defaults
plugins.description: Opt-in steering: opinionated default stack choices for frontend, infrastructure, and quality/observability. Install to adopt these defaults when setting up or standardizing a project.

plugins.name: steering-tools-scripts
plugins.description: Opinionated conventions for repo tooling and automation: where scripts, generators, maintained CLIs, and task runners live and how they are structured. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: token-savings
plugins.description: Context-cost reduction for Claude and Codex, with the measurement instrument that decides whether the reduction is real. A PreToolUse guard routes selected read-only commands through rtk, scoped to an allowlist verified to preserve content, and a second denies reading a repomix pack (six context windows on a large repository) while naming the rg and awk that search it. Oversized shell output spills to a file with its recovery commands. The tokenmeter A/B harness measures runs from transcript usage records instead of a tool's self-report, and repomix-tune re-derives every pack-filtering claim on the installed repomix. Telemetry stays off. Requires python3 on PATH; rtk and repomix are optional and every path degrades to a no-op without them.

plugins.name: toolchain-cache-policy
plugins.description: Shares bounded package-manager and compiler caches across worktrees without redirecting mutable dependencies or branch output into machine-global directories. SessionStart uses DEVELOPMENT_CACHE_HOME for sccache, Python, Go, Node, Deno, Gradle, NuGet, Trivy, Restic, and lint cache paths, then evicts only regenerable compiler caches under disk pressure. Cargo targets remain repository-scoped through Worktrunk. Fails open; Claude and Codex SessionStart parity.

plugins.name: typescript-quality
plugins.description: Run TypeScript or JavaScript format, lint, type-check, and test commands with the project toolchain.

plugins.name: user-journeys
plugins.description: Service-agnostic user-journey lifecycle: author end-to-end journeys as living documents (current-truth body plus a windowed delta log), validate them against the running product through whatever interface it exposes (web, desktop via MCP, CLI, TUI, API), triage mismatches with intent-gated amendment authority, report findings through a pluggable reporter (GitHub issues or a local tracker), and run multi-journey campaigns with a bounded dispatch-coder fix loop. Ships six skills (init, write, verify, verify-changed, consolidate, campaign), two agents (journey-scribe, journey-validator), agent-only and human-gated Beads verification formulas, the journey format spec and templates, and deterministic index, lint, and formula-install scripts.

plugins.name: verify
plugins.description: Run and report a final local verification pass (tests, types, build, lint) before handoff, commit, push, merge, or PR.

plugins.name: web-fetch
plugins.description: Retrieve current or URL-specific information from the web with source-aware tool routing for fetching, browsing, citing, and verifying online.

plugins.name: whats-new
plugins.description: Research what changed in a tool, CLI, library, framework, package, or dependency -- or a technology, cloud service, hosted API, platform, or model family (AWS Bedrock, Anthropic/Claude, OpenAI, GCP, Azure, …) -- between what is in use and the latest: breaking changes, deprecations, new features, and fixes. Resolves versions, repos, changelogs, release notes, commit logs, and service announcement feeds/APIs via machine endpoints instead of reading rendered pages, then summarizes into a fixed template.

plugins.name: worktrunk-writer
plugins.description: Reusable Worktrunk writer lifecycle for Claude and Codex. Pre-creates named worktrees, copies only allowlisted ignored files, records a branch lease, validates writer paths before mutation, consumes Worktrunk schema-2 JSON fleet evidence, and delegates merge and removal safety to Worktrunk. Beads metadata is joined when the repository has an active beads workspace. Worktrunk's native plugins remain the owner of runtime activity markers and lifecycle events.

plugins.name: write-agentic
plugins.description: Author or update skills, steering, or agent definitions using standard machine-language templates and a lint script that validates them.
